A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide complete, readable main texts and appendices. Methods, equations, figures and results can be matched across renaming and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, a 34-participant user study, and supplementary clustering and CelebA analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports a 50-participant user study, additional baseline results and clustering-accuracy measurements.

M1.justification: V1 Section 3.5 already retrains the last layer using ablated images. V2 incorporates this existing component into ASM, matching v1's SCM + DFR, while SCM becomes the variant without retraining. The PDFs do not establish changes to clustering, prototype selection, KNN classification or token ablation.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ISIC, knee radiographs, ImageNet-W and the CelebA analysis. The expanded Waterbirds discussion in Appendix C supplies results attributed to prior work, not evidence of newly evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds SUBG as an evaluated comparator for all three datasets in Table 1. The unmitigated baseline, DFR and JTT remain; renaming the proposed variants does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: The user-study sample increases from 34 to 50 participants in Section 5.3. Appendix D introduces a clustering-accuracy assessment. The main benchmark splits, ViT-B-16 configuration and worst/average-group accuracy measures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds quantitative clustering-accuracy checks across the three benchmarks and specifies manual validation of 200 ISIC prototype patches. The two-versus-three-cluster comparison and CelebA examples are retained. The retraining comparison already existed before being described explicitly as an ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three sequential seeds and report benchmark means and standard deviations. Both user studies report mean, standard deviation and a one-tailed t-test against 51.3% chance. Changed sample size and statistical values do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds SUBG results, including worst-group accuracies of 52.7%, 47.7% and 80.3%. New Table 4 reports clustering accuracies of 76.0%, 100.0% and 91.6%. The expanded user study reports 91.2% accuracy versus 86.8%, with t(49)=15.33 replacing t(33)=1670.7647. Existing matched benchmark, masking and overclustering scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The embedding, distance, homogeneity, Brier-score and KNN-ablation formulas retain their substance. Relabeling D(p) as P(p) and numbering the selection equation clarify notation without changing the equal-weight selection rule. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the contribution framed as competitive SCM plus state-of-the-art DFR integration with a full ASM pipeline claimed to outperform group-annotated methods. It emphasizes direct removal of shortcut features. The abstract and overarching efficiency, interpretability and shortcut-mitigation claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly acknowledges unavailable ground-truth shortcut-location annotations and qualifies validation as manual inspection. The discussion adds implications for transformer-specific benchmarks. The existing limitation concerning multiple interacting shortcuts and CelebA is retained, moving into the conclusion.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies retraining of the last dense layer on post-ablation embeddings without group annotations. Appendix C newly states that CelebA fine-tuning uses the same hyperparameters as the other datasets. Hardware, data-construction instructions, LLM prompts and the code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Idrissi et al.'s SUBG work and expands discussion of the already cited transformer-robustness research. It revises DFR's description to group-balanced last-layer retraining and positions its own retraining step as distinct from, rather than analogous to, DFR.

P1.justification: V2 makes widespread sentence-level copyedits, renames SCM to ASM, moves retraining into Section 3.4.3 and relocates limitations to the conclusion. It updates authorship and acknowledgments and integrates appendix references, while retaining the overall narrative and section structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised to depict the automatic route and last-layer retraining. Table 1 adds SUBG rows and reorganizes the proposed variants; Appendix D gains Table 4. Supplementary formatting removes placeholder authors and integrates numbering. Existing prototype images and concept-description displays are retained.

improvement.justification: SUBG comparisons and clustering diagnostics modestly strengthen validation. The larger user study now reports a t statistic consistent with its stated mean, standard deviation and sample size, unlike v1. Retraining is also described more clearly. These gains are limited: main benchmark findings remain unchanged, and the conclusion's no-retraining wording remains poorly aligned with the emphasized last-layer step.
